( D ) Higher context specificity during reversal predicted reinstatement during test old , as a function of CS type: ( Di ) Higher reversal context specificity predicted more pronounced generalized reinstatement of CS+- vs. CS-+ acquisition memory traces in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC)/superior frontal gyrus (SFG) (left), and reversely, more pronounced generalized reinstatement of CS-+ vs. CS+- acquisition memory traces in the precuneus (right).
We extracted subject-wise measures of context specificity from the PFC cluster in Figure 4B and compared them to both item reinstatement and generalized reinstatement.
We used LME models with ‘context specificity’ and ‘cue type’ as predictors and ‘item reinstatement’ or ‘generalized reinstatement’ as the dependent variable ( Figure 5C ).

Interestingly, representations from the first test phase were less reinstated during the second test phase (despite the fact that both test phases occurred during the second experimental day), compared with acquisition and reversal traces formed on the first experimental day ( Figure 4E ).

This suggests that for these cues, the more distinct the contextual encoding during reversal, the more strongly the original fear memory trace resurfaced, likely reflecting a return of fear ( Figure 5D ).
